result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers have well-built type scales with sensible body sizes, tighter heading line-heights and mobile h1 reductions of about 75–78%. Answer A never caps the article width, so it fails the 60–75 character rule; Answer B sets 65ch on paragraphs. B's 14px code is a slightly bigger drop below its 17px desktop body than ideal, and its line-heights are hard-coded rather than custom properties, but the missing width cap in A matters more. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers have well-built, paste-ready scales: body text at 17px on desktop and 16px on mobile, headings tighter than body with a clear step from h2 to h3, a mobile h1 at about three-quarters of desktop, and custom properties throughout. B never caps the line length, so on wide screens the text can stretch far past 75 characters; A limits paragraphs, list items and captions to 65ch. B's code and caption sizes follow body size a bit more closely, but that does not outweigh the missing line-length cap.
